keyConcepts.title: Wireless vs. mobility
keyConcepts.text: **Wireless** is about communicating over a radio link. **Mobility** is about keeping connections working while a device changes where it's attached to the network. They're separate problems.

keyConcepts.title: Elements of a wireless network
keyConcepts.text: Wireless hosts, wireless links, base stations (cell towers, access points) and the network infrastructure. Networks are **infrastructure-based** or **ad hoc**, and **single-hop** or **multi-hop**.

keyConcepts.title: Why wireless links are harder
keyConcepts.text: Path loss, interference and multipath make bit errors common. Higher **SNR** means lower **BER**; faster modulation has a higher BER at the same SNR, so rates adapt to conditions.

keyConcepts.title: Hidden terminals and CDMA
keyConcepts.text: Two stations that can't hear each other can still collide at the receiver. **CDMA** gives each sender an orthogonal code so several can transmit at once.

keyConcepts.title: 802.11 WiFi basics
keyConcepts.text: A BSS is an AP plus its stations. APs send beacons; devices scan passively or actively, then associate and use DHCP. Channels 1, 6 and 11 don't overlap.

keyConcepts.title: CSMA/CA
keyConcepts.text: Sense the channel, wait DIFS, count down a random backoff only while the channel is idle, send the whole frame, then wait for an **ACK** after SIFS. Optional **RTS/CTS** reserves the channel.

keyConcepts.title: The 802.11 frame
keyConcepts.text: Four address fields: receiver, transmitter, the **router interface** (address 3) and one for ad hoc use. Sequence numbers catch duplicates; the duration field supports reservations.

keyConcepts.title: Bluetooth
keyConcepts.text: A short-range, low-power cable replacement. A piconet has one controller and up to 7 active clients, using frequency hopping across 79 channels.

keyConcepts.title: 4G/5G cellular architecture
keyConcepts.text: UE (with IMSI on a SIM), base station (eNode-B), **HSS** and **MME** (control plane), and **S-GW/P-GW** (data plane, using GTP tunnels). 5G adds millimeter wave, small cells and slicing.

keyConcepts.title: Mobility management
keyConcepts.text: A home network with a permanent address and a visited network with a care-of address. **Indirect routing** goes through the home agent (triangle routing); **direct routing** sends to the care-of address.

keyConcepts.title: Handover and impact on TCP
keyConcepts.text: The source base station hands the device to the target, and the tunnel is moved. TCP mistakes wireless losses for congestion; fixes are **local recovery**, **sender awareness** and **split connections**.

flashcards.back: Sends and receives data for the wireless hosts associated with it, e.g. a cell tower or WiFi access point.
Infrastructure: hosts connect through a base station to a larger network. Ad hoc: no infrastructure, and hosts handle routing themselves.
A mobile host changing which base station it's attached to.
Path loss (decreasing signal strength), interference from other sources, and multipath propagation.
Signal-to-noise ratio, measured in dB. Higher SNR makes the signal easier to extract from noise.
For a given modulation, higher SNR means lower BER. At a given SNR, a faster modulation has a higher BER.
A and C both send to B but can't hear each other (an obstacle or fading), so they collide at B without knowing.

flashcards.front: How does CDMA allow simultaneous senders?
flashcards.back: Each sender multiplies its bits by its own orthogonal code. A receiver decodes with the sender's code (inner product ÷ M), and other senders' signals cancel out.
BSS: an access point plus its wireless stations. SSID: the network name the AP advertises.
Passive: listen for AP beacon frames. Active: broadcast a probe request and wait for probe responses.

flashcards.front: Why doesn't WiFi use collision detection?
flashcards.back: A device can't easily hear weak incoming signals while transmitting, and hidden terminals and fading would hide collisions anyway.
If idle, send after DIFS. Otherwise pick a random backoff and count down only while idle; send at 0, wait for ACK; with no ACK, back off from a larger range.
SIFS: short wait before a receiver sends an ACK. DIFS: longer idle wait before a station starts sending.
The sender sends Request to Send; the AP broadcasts Clear to Send, which reserves the channel and tells others to stay quiet. It helps with hidden terminals.
1: the receiving station. 2: the transmitting station. 3: the MAC address of the router interface the subnet connects through.
Two missing ACKs in a row: drop to the next lower rate. Ten ACKs in a row: try the next higher rate.
A node sleeps between beacons; the AP buffers its frames and lists them in the beacon. A node can sleep about 99% of the time.
One controller plus up to 7 active clients (and up to 255 parked devices), using frequency-hopping spread spectrum over 79 channels.
The IMSI is the subscriber's identity, stored on the SIM card. It identifies the user and their home carrier.
Home Subscriber Server: a control-plane database of subscribers, used for authentication.
Mobility Management Entity: control plane. It handles authentication with the HSS, sets up tunnels and tracks which cell a device is in.
Data-plane gateways. The P-GW gives the device its IP address (and NAT) and is the gateway to the Internet.

flashcards.front: What carries user data between the base station and the gateways?
flashcards.back: GTP tunnels (GPRS Tunneling Protocol, over UDP).
OFDM: each device gets 0.5 ms time slots on one or more frequencies, chosen by the operator's scheduler.
eMBB (enhanced mobile broadband), URLLC (ultra-reliable low latency, about 1 ms) and mMTC (massive IoT).
Very high data rates, but short range and poor wall penetration, so 5G needs many small cells and beamforming.
Permanent: the device's fixed address in its home network. Care-of: its address in the visited network.
With indirect routing, packets go correspondent → home agent → visited network, even when a shorter route exists.
It isn't transparent: the correspondent must learn the care-of address and be updated when the device moves.

flashcards.front: Why does TCP perform poorly over wireless?
flashcards.back: It treats every loss as congestion and cuts cwnd, even when the loss came from bit errors or a handover.
Break the end-to-end connection into a wireless part (mobile ↔ base station) and a wired part, each with its own transport connection.

quiz.q: What is the main difference between wireless and mobility?
options: Wireless is about the radio link; mobility is about changing the point of attachment
Wireless only applies to cellular networks
quiz.explain: A device can be wireless without moving, and a wired laptop can move between networks.

quiz.q: For a given modulation scheme, what happens to BER as SNR increases?
quiz.explain: A stronger signal relative to noise means fewer bit errors, at the cost of more transmit power.

quiz.q: Stations A and C can't hear each other but both send to B at the same time. What is this called?
quiz.explain: Their signals collide at B, but carrier sensing can't detect it. RTS/CTS helps.

quiz.q: Which set of 2.4 GHz channels don't overlap?
quiz.explain: Channels must be 4 or more apart to avoid overlapping; 1, 6 and 11 is the only set of three.

quiz.q: Why does 802.11 use collision avoidance instead of collision detection?
options: It's hard to detect collisions while transmitting, and hidden terminals hide them
quiz.explain: So 802.11 avoids collisions with random backoff (and optional RTS/CTS) and uses link-layer ACKs.

quiz.q: In CSMA/CA, when does a station count down its backoff timer?
options: Only while the channel is sensed idle
Always, even when the channel is busy
quiz.explain: The counter freezes while the channel is busy, so the station with the smaller backoff wins and the other waits.

quiz.q: What does an AP's CTS frame do?
options: Gives the sender permission and tells other stations not to send for the reserved time
quiz.explain: Every station hears the CTS, so even hidden stations stay quiet during the reserved period.

quiz.q: What does address 3 in an 802.11 frame hold?
options: The MAC address of the router interface
quiz.explain: It lets the AP convert between 802.11 and Ethernet frames, since the AP is just a link-layer device.

quiz.q: In 4G LTE, which element is a control-plane database used to authenticate subscribers?
quiz.explain: The HSS stores subscriber information and works with the MME for authentication.

quiz.q: Which 4G element assigns IP addresses to mobile devices and connects to the Internet?
quiz.explain: The P-GW is the last LTE element before the Internet and hides device mobility from the outside world.

quiz.q: Which 5G service type targets about 1 ms latency?
quiz.explain: Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communications is for things like factory automation and self-driving cars.

quiz.q: What is the main drawback of indirect routing to a mobile device?
options: Triangle routing: packets detour through the home network
The correspondent must know the care-of address
quiz.explain: Indirect routing is transparent to the correspondent, but it can be inefficient.

quiz.q: In a 4G handover, what does the MME reconfigure?
options: The S-GW-to-base-station tunnel, so it ends at the target base station
quiz.explain: After the target base station accepts the device, the MME moves the tunnel to it.

quiz.q: Why can TCP perform badly over wireless links?
options: It treats losses from bit errors or handovers as congestion and slows down
It uses too few sequence numbers
quiz.explain: Fixes include link-layer recovery (ARQ/FEC), wireless-aware TCP and split connections.
